title: Willingness to Pay
statement: Working mothers aged 28–40 (or their employers) will pay [$/₹X] per month for emotional support from a single platform, rather than relying on free options like friends, WhatsApp groups, and Instagram communities.
realWorldAnalogy: Example: Drivers will use their personal cars to earn money / People will pay to sleep in an unlicensed stranger's spare room.
howWeTestIt: Prototype simulated checkout tier selector ($9/mo vs ₹749/mo vs $29/session) testing actual price reservation intent without charging credit cards.
keyRisk: Women may default to free WhatsApp or Instagram DMs unless the emotional buddy provides immediate structure and zero-guilt accountability.

title: Trust and Disclosure
statement: Women in our starting segment will share a real, vulnerable problem (not a surface-level one) with an AI-guided, women-only platform within their first week, without a human they already know vouching for it.
realWorldAnalogy: Example: People will get into a car with a stranger who isn't a licensed taxi driver (Uber).
howWeTestIt: 5–10 second live video check by a female assistant + zero-knowledge pseudonym generation. Vulnerability depth is measured via word length and sentiment distress analysis.
keyRisk: Fear of surveillance or identity leakage if video verification feels intrusive rather than reassuring.

title: Repeat Use & Habit Formation
statement: Women will come back on their own at least weekly for 4+ weeks, because the pain is frequent enough to build a habit and not just a one-time need during a crisis.
realWorldAnalogy: Example: People will check Instagram multiple times daily to see peer stories, not just once a month.
howWeTestIt: Evening WhatsApp check-ins (8 PM OpenWA prompt), multi-day emotional streak tracking, and personalized emotional trajectory charts in the profile drawer.
keyRisk: Users might only vent during acute emotional fires and forget the app once the panic subsides.

title: Single Specific Job Chosen First
statement: Women in one life stage will choose us for one specific job, such as "talk to someone who understands within minutes when I'm overwhelmed," over therapy apps, communities, or content they already use, and an integrated platform is not required on day one.
realWorldAnalogy: Example: People opened Uber just to "push a button and get a ride in 3 minutes", not for full mobility services.
howWeTestIt: Instant 60-second structured CBT venting and somatic grounding chamber without onboarding friction or mandatory phone sign-up.
keyRisk: Feature creep distracting from the instant emotional first-aid core experience.

title: Community Liveliness & Safe Moderation
statement: A women-only peer community can reach self-sustaining activity (at least [20%] of members posting or replying weekly) at a moderation cost that is safe and affordable.
realWorldAnalogy: Example: Reddit subreddits rely on volunteer/automated moderation with high community self-policing.
howWeTestIt: Anonymous life-stage circles with peer hugs, verified sisterhood badge, and automated AI routing to similar women based on distress keywords.
keyRisk: Lurker bias where 90% read and <10% post unless psychological safety and anonymity are strictly guaranteed.
